# Kushmanda — Sati's own language model (`sati-kushmanda-v3`)

decoder-only transformer: RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU, fused causal attention, tied embeddings, **34.1M parameters**, trained from random initialisation on `cuda`: 4,000 pretraining steps, then 2,000 instruction-tuning steps.

**Corpus** (cleaned and deduplicated): 427,826 documents — mitre-attack 3,652, mitre-attack-procedure 14,431, mitre-capec 1,207, mitre-cwe 917, cisa-kev 1,690, repository 361, nvd-cve 372,742, mitre-attack-mobile 455, mitre-attack-ics 490, github-advisory 31,881. 21,482 held out by document; 47,912,771 training tokens.

## Answering from given passages — held out by entity

22,616 training pairs. 1,200 of 1,462 held-out questions are scored here, all about techniques, CVEs and CWEs never seen in tuning. Each question comes with 3 passages; in about 10% of them none holds the answer, and the right reply is to say so. Held-out answer loss: 0.2029.

*Copy precision* is the share of the answer's word 4-grams found in its passages. A grounded answer scores high; one written from memory scores low. The lexical baseline answers with a whole passage, so its copy precision is 1 by construction.

## Free completions

A small, narrow model: it knows the domain's language, but it is not a source of facts. That's why Sati never treats generated text as evidence (rule 1).
